title: A create whose podman run fails leaves its two volumes, and ls then lists a sandbox nobody removed
foundBy: session agent, 2026-11-16, while a gVisor experiment's `create --privileged` failed at `podman run`
stint: gvisor branch, session agent, 2026-11-17, the owner's ask

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/engine/ -count=1 -run TestPodmanCreateReapsAFailedRun: 6 subtests PASS, for a fresh name, data kept by rm and a name already held, each on podman and gvisor. On the code before the fix the 4 fresh-name and kept-data subtests fail. On this host, with a stand-in runsc that refuses every container: the build before the fix left cs-sandbox-home-b1.sbx125old, cs-sandbox-containers-b1.sbx125old and a Created container, and ls listed b1 as removed. The fixed build left no volume and no container, and ls listed nothing. A failed create over data that rm kept left both volumes and the marker file in the home. make ci passed over the working tree that became af200a5 and a8cbb28.

resolution: Fixed. Create arms its reap before `podman run` rather than after it, and first asks whether a container already holds the name. A failed run then removes the container and the data volumes it made. It keeps volumes an earlier `rm` kept, and leaves a container it found. SPEC R179 states the rule.
details:
`Podman.Create` (internal/engine/podman.go) returns as soon as `podman run` fails. The deferred reap that removes a partial sandbox is armed only after the run succeeds. Podman has already created the named volumes the run mounts by then, `cs-sandbox-home-<name>.<group>` and `cs-sandbox-containers-<name>.<group>`, so both stay. `ls` reads a home volume with no instance as data `rm` kept, and lists the name as `removed`.

Seen on 2026-11-16 in an experiment group: `create gp1 --group gvexp2 --privileged` under gVisor failed at `podman run`, and `group rm gvexp2 -f` then left both volumes. To reproduce, make `podman run` fail after it has parsed its volumes, for example with a runtime that refuses the container. A create that never ran should leave nothing behind, so the reap belongs before the run, scoped to volumes this create made (`reusingData` already tells the two apart).

notes.text: a8cbb28 is on the local gvisor branch, which is neither pushed nor merged. The fix is in the podman engine's create, so podman and gVisor sandboxes both have it.

The branch was rebased onto main at b9ee8bb, and this record now cites the rebased commits. The verification above ran on the same changes before the rebase. Over 3c10458, the rebased branch, `make ci` passed. There, `go test ./internal/engine/ -count=1 -run TestPodmanCreateReapsAFailedRun -v` passed all six subtests.
